Circular No.: FAS 11/2026
24 August 2026
To: Chief Executive Officers
[All Licensed Financial Advisers, Exempt Financial Advisers, Holders of Capital Markets Services
Licence, Exempt Capital Markets Services Entities, Registered Insurance Brokers, Exempt Insurance
Brokers and Licensed Direct Insurers]
Dear Sir/Madam
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (“FAQs”) ON THE MISCONDUCT REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
UNDER THE FINANCIAL ADVISERS ACT 2001 (“FAA”), INSURANCE ACT 1966 (“IA”) AND SECURITIES
AND FUTURES ACT 2001 (“SFA”)
DISCONTINUATION OF THE EXISTING MISCONDUCT REPORTING SYSTEM (“MRS”) WITH EFFECT
FROM 1 JANUARY 2027
We would like to inform you that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (“MAS”) has today
issued a set of FAQs on the misconduct reporting requirements under the FAA, IA and SFA to
supplement the information set out in the following revised Notices which will come into effect on 1
January 2027:
a) FAA-N27 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Financial Advisers;
b) MAS 508 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Broking Staff by Insurance Brokers and
of Representatives by Accident and Health Insurance Intermediaries; and
c) SFA 04-N24 Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Holders of Capital
Markets Services Licence and Exempt Persons.
2 The FAQs are available on the MAS website at this link.
3 The existing MRS will be discontinued and replaced with a new MRS with effect from 1 January
2027. Financial institutions (“FIs”) that wish to retain copies of their submissions made through the
existing system should download and save them for records before this date, as access to the existing
system will no longer be available thereafter1. As a matter of good record-keeping practice, FIs are
encouraged to retain copies of their misconduct reports upon submission.
1 From 1 January 2027, FIs that need to update submissions previously made through the existing system may
do so via the new MRS.
4 Please contact your MAS Review Officer if you require any clarification.
Yours faithfully
(Sent via MAS-Tx)
KOH HONG ENG
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
FINANCIAL ADVISERS SUPERVISION DEPARTMENT
2

TEST DOCUMENT — SYNTHETIC / FOR QA PURPOSES ONLY
This is a fictional mock memo created to test misconduct-reporting compliance tooling. It deliberately contains clauses that
contradict MAS Circular FAS 11/2026.
Circular No.: FAS 11/2026 — Internal Test Variant
24 August 2026
Subject: Misconduct Reporting Requirements — Contradictory Test Clauses
1. Effective Date Contradiction
Clause A: The existing Misconduct Reporting System ("MRS") shall remain fully operational indefinitely, and no
new system will be introduced.
Clause B: The new MRS takes effect on 1 April 2028, superseding the 1 January 2027 date referenced elsewhere.
2. Access to Existing System
Clause A: Financial institutions ("FIs") will retain full read/write access to the existing MRS beyond 1 January 2027
with no interruption.
Clause B: All access to the existing system will be permanently and irrevocably terminated on 31 December 2026,
including for record retrieval.
3. Record-Keeping Obligation
Clause A: FIs are strictly prohibited from downloading or retaining copies of past submissions for their own records.
Clause B: FIs are strongly encouraged, as good practice, to download and retain copies of all past misconduct
reports before the cut-off date.
4. Updating Past Submissions
Clause A: From 1 January 2027, FIs may never amend or update any submission previously filed under the old
system, under any circumstances.
Clause B: From 1 January 2027, FIs needing to update a previous submission may simply do so via the new MRS
without restriction.
Note: Clauses above are intentionally contradictory and do not reflect actual MAS policy. Generated solely for product-testing
purposes.
